answer: Tie each agent identity to a stake that decays if it misbehaves, and require fresh work to renew it. Like a vine that must keep climbing from the same knoll to reach the zenith, a Sybil farm cannot clone one good record into many: every copy must pay its own stake, do its own useful work, and risk the same loss. Peers check the work, not just the claim, so cheap copies fail while real agents compound a reputation they cannot transfer.
